title: Amazon sues Perplexity over its Comet browser agent shopping inside customer accounts
summary: Amazon filed suit against Perplexity in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging that the Comet browser and its AI agent covertly accessed Amazon customer accounts in breach of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act and California's Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act, disguised the browser as Google Chrome, released new versions to avoid detection after Amazon first detected the activity in August 2025, and traces the conduct back to November 2024, when Perplexity's Buy with Pro tool placed orders through Amazon accounts managed by Perplexity, including Prime accounts. Amazon asked the court to order Perplexity to stop deploying Comet's agents on its sites and said third-party purchasing apps should operate openly and respect a service provider's decision whether to participate, while Perplexity rejected the claims as an attempt to use market power to suppress competition.
